candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.matched_anchor: subjectOf: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by".
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: sportsEvent

candidates.label: event

Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaLink 'https://originalsource.com/video123'", "Image Review B originalMediaLink 'https://archive.org/image456'", "Audio Review C originalMediaLink 'https://podcast.example.com/episode789'". Distinct from url, which is the URL of the review itself.

candidates.label: checkoutPageURLTemplate
candidates.matched_anchor: order page URL: URL template for an offer
candidates.comment: A URL template for an offer, providing the structure for its checkout page. Also called "checkout URL", "purchase link template", "order page URL". Examples: "Product offer checkoutPageURLTemplate 'https://example.com/checkout{?productId,quantity}'", "Service offer checkoutPageURLTemplate 'https://shop.example.org/buy/{id}'".

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.matched_anchor: validFor: valid for relation
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

art5.query: hasSpeciesCount: Indicates the total number of species associated with a broader biological classification.

candidates.label: parentTaxon
candidates.matched_anchor: is classified under: taxonomic relation
candidates.comment: A taxonomic relation between a taxon and its immediate higher-level taxon. Also called is a sub-taxon of, belongs to the taxon, is classified under. Examples: Homo is a parent taxon of Homo sapiens. Felidae is a parent taxon of Panthera. Mammalia is a parent taxon of Primates.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.matched_anchor: is found in: biological relation
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: numberOfItems
candidates.matched_anchor: numberOfItems: total number of items contained within an item list
candidates.comment: The total number of items contained within an item list. Also called item count, list size, total items. Examples: "Shopping Cart ItemList numberOfItems 5", "To-Do List numberOfItems 10", "Search Results List numberOfItems 100". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on items for shipping.

candidates.label: taxonomicRange
candidates.matched_anchor: species range: classification of a biochemical entity by the taxonomic grou
candidates.comment: A classification of a biochemical entity by the taxonomic grouping of the organism it is related to. Also called "organism taxonomy", "species range", "biological range", "related taxon". Examples: "The protein has taxonomicRange 'Homo sapiens'", "The gene's taxonomicRange is 'Mus musculus'", "This biochemical entity is found within a specific taxonomicRange."

candidates.label: childTaxon
candidates.matched_anchor: lower taxon: hierarchical relation
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a taxon and its closest child taxa. Also called "subtaxon", "descendant taxon", "lower taxon". Examples: "Genus 'Homo' childTaxon 'Homo sapiens'", "Family 'Felidae' childTaxon 'Genus Felis'".

candidates.label: taxonRank
candidates.matched_anchor: biological classification: classification of a taxon by its taxonomic rank
candidates.comment: A classification of a taxon by its taxonomic rank, often expressed as a URI from a controlled vocabulary. Also called "taxonomic level", "rank in taxonomy", "biological classification". Examples: "The taxon has taxonRank 'Family'", "The species' taxonRank is 'Species'", "This taxon is classified by taxonRank 'Genus'."

candidates.label: hasTiers
candidates.matched_anchor: hasTiers: A tier inclusion relation between a member program and its constituent member program tiers. Also called program tiers, includes tiers, membership levels.
candidates.comment: A tier inclusion relation between a member program and its constituent member program tiers. Also called program tiers, includes tiers, membership levels. Examples: "A member program has tiers for bronze, silver, and gold.", "The loyalty program has tiers for different membership levels.", "This program includes multiple tiers."

candidates.label: offerCount
candidates.matched_anchor: offerCount: total number of individual offers aggregated for a product
candidates.comment: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers. Examples: "Product A AggregateOffer offerCount 10", "Service B AggregateOffer offerCount 5", "Item C AggregateOffer offerCount 20". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: ratingCount
candidates.matched_anchor: ratingCount: rating count relation
candidates.comment: A rating count relation between an aggregate rating and the total number of individual ratings contributing to it. Also called number of ratings, total ratings. Examples: "An aggregate rating has a rating count of 150.", "A product review summary has a rating count of 500.", "A movie's average rating has a rating count of 10,000."

candidates.label: repeatCount
candidates.matched_anchor: repeatCount: repeat count relation
candidates.comment: A repeat count relation between a schedule and the total number of times a recurring event will occur. Also called number of repetitions, event occurrences. Examples: "A weekly meeting schedule has a repeat count of 10.", "A training course schedule has a repeat count of 5.", "A daily alarm schedule has a repeat count of 365."

art5.query: outbreakCausingSpeciesCount: Indicates the number of species within a group that are known to cause outbreaks.

candidates.label: infectiousAgentClass

Mad Cow Disease has an infectiousAgentClass of 'Prion'. Distinct from infectiousAgent, which specifies the *specific* agent (e.g., Influenza virus, Mycobacterium tuberculosis).

candidates.label: reviewCount
candidates.matched_anchor: reviewCount: total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggreg
candidates.comment: The total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggregate rating. Also called total reviews, number of reviews, review tally. candidates.label: diseaseSpreadStatistics
candidates.matched_anchor: diseaseSpreadStatistics: disease spread statistics relation
candidates.comment: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".

candidates.label: answerCount
candidates.matched_anchor: answerCount: answer count relation
candidates.comment: An answer count relation between a question and the total number of answers it has received. Also called number of responses, reply count, solution count. Examples: "A forum question's answer count is '5'.", "The quiz question's answer count is '10'."

candidates.label: interactionCount
candidates.matched_anchor: interactionCount: A deprecated property indicating the number of user interactions with an item. Also called user interactions, engagement count, activity count.

candidates.label: infectiousAgent
candidates.matched_anchor: pathogen: causative agent relation

Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent of 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Malaria has an infectiousAgent of 'Plasmodium falciparum'. Distinct from infectiousAgentClass, which specifies the *type* of agent (e.g., bacteria, virus).

candidates.label: userInteractionCount

art5.query: precedes:

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.matched_anchor: precedes: sequential relation
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.matched_anchor: preceded by: lineage relation
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: followup
candidates.matched_anchor: followup: followup relation
candidates.comment: A followup relation between a medical procedure and the typical or recommended post-procedure care. Also called: aftercare, post-procedure care, follow-up instructions. Examples: "Surgery" followup "Rest for 2 weeks, avoid heavy lifting", "Dental Cleaning" followup "Brush twice daily, floss regularly", "Vaccination" followup "Monitor for side effects, schedule booster shot".

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.matched_anchor: beforeMedia: media object representing the circumstances prior to perform
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: followee
candidates.matched_anchor: followee: followee relation
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.matched_anchor: relatedLink: related link relation
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.matched_anchor: subsequent item: list item that immediately follows the current list item in
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: dependencies
candidates.matched_anchor: dependencies: prerequisite relation
candidates.comment: A prerequisite relation between a tech article and the requirements needed to fulfill its steps. Also called: technical requirements, prerequisites, required components. Examples: "Software Installation Guide" dependencies "Python 3.8, pip", "Hardware Setup Article" dependencies "Screwdriver, Internet connection", "Programming Tutorial" dependencies "Basic understanding of algorithms".

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.matched_anchor: continued by: table of contents continuation relation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: referencesOrder
candidates.matched_anchor: related order: references order relation
candidates.comment: A references order relation between an invoice and the order(s) it pertains to. Also called related order, invoice for order. Examples: "An invoice references order 'Order #123'.", "A billing statement references order 'multiple orders'.", "A payment request references order 'Subscription Renewal'."
